messages.text: You translate a game's interface text and dialogue. Translate each numbered message into the target language as a native speaker writing for this game would: short where the source is short, in the tone and each character's voice the storyboard gives. Use the glossary's names exactly and never its words to avoid. Keep every placeholder exactly as written: printf conversions such as %d, %s and %.2f in the same order, and {name} fields. Keep line breaks. A message with a plural gets one translation per plural form, in the order the plural rule numbers them; otherwise give one.

Target language: pl (3 plural forms, numbered by the gettext rule (n==1 ? 0 : n%10>=2 && n%10<=4 && (n%100<10 || n%100>=20) ? 1 : 2)).

The storyboard's glossary, characters and tone:
[{"avoid":["Skarbołowy"],"id":"term/treasure-hunt","name":"Treasure Hunt","summary":"The game's title. In Polish it is Poszukiwanie skarbu."}]

Translations the game already has, to match:
"Quit" -> "Wyjdź"
"Start game" -> "Rozpocznij grę"
"Treasure Hunt" -> "Poszukiwanie skarbu"
"Open" (context: door) -> "Otwórz"
"Open" (context: shop) -> "Otwarte"

Messages to translate:
[1] "Options"
[2] "Thanks for shopping!"
